_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 11 When Networks Fail. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order (a network failure; what stops; encryption; where and why; why anyone bothers to encrypt), and every word is from lesson-11.py: its four causes, its three places, its six encrypted things and its bus timetable. Computing keeps no ART.sim and the lesson's network activity is a closure, so the network is drawn here in the engine's idiom - nothing technical is added, no message hops or is routed, and the only things crossed out are the broken link and the app that stopped, never a person.
title: When Networks Fail
subtitle: Grade 4 Computing
objectives: Identify issues that may occur as a result of a failure in a network.
Identify where and why encryption is used in digital systems.

beats.say: A cable is cut. The router dies. The network has failed.
What stops working? And where does encryption keep data safe?

at.enc: where does encryption keep data safe

beats.say: A network failure is any break in the connection between devices.
A router with no power. A cut cable. A server switched off.
Or the wi-fi password is changed. Any of these breaks the link.
Some children think a failure means the computers are broken.
They are not. The computers are fine. They just cannot reach each other.
Everything that needed another device stops. Start at school.
Nothing prints. Saved work on the server cannot be opened.
The register cannot be sent. Now the shop: the till cannot ask the bank.

at.till: the till cannot ask the bank

beats.say: So it is cash only. At home videos stop and calls drop.
The smart speaker goes quiet. All of them needed another device.

at.speaker: The smart speaker goes quiet
at.all: All of them needed another device

beats.say: Writing a story carries on. The calculator carries on. They need nobody else.
Encryption scrambles data so only someone with the key can read it.
Data on a network passes through many devices on its way.
Anyone who grabs it in the middle sees only nonsense.
Some children think encryption hides that a message was sent.
It hides what the message says. They may see it went, and cannot read it.
Your password is encrypted before it leaves your device.
A card number when you pay. A private message to a friend.
A medical record. The padlock in the browser: that connection is encrypted.
The password on your wi-fi encrypts what travels through the air.
Anything that would do harm if a stranger read it is encrypted.

at.harm: do harm if a stranger read it

beats.say: A bus timetable is not, because anyone may read it.
Cybercrime is crime done through computers and networks.
Stealing data. Locking somebody's files and demanding money.
Pretending to be a bank to get a password. Encryption is the main defence.
A thief takes a laptop full of encrypted records. They have taken a brick.
The data is there and unreadable. That is why hospitals and schools encrypt.
A network failure breaks the links, not the devices.
The server is out of reach, so saved work cannot be opened.
Encryption scrambles data, and only the key unscrambles it.
Look for the padlock. Encryption is the main defence against cybercrime.
